subject: Salem Street Corridor Rezoning
overview: The commission adjudicated multiple demolition delay cases and significant property determinations, finding 4 Grove Street preferably preserved while allowing 31 Wilson Street to proceed to demolition. Members also allocated funding for veteran monument restoration and discussed strategies to protect historic resources in light of proposed city rezoning.

items.title: 140 Summer Street
items.summary: Tabled the hearing for 30 days because the property did not meet signage and legal advertisement requirements.

items.title: 31 Wilson Street
items.summary: Found the property not preferably preserved, allowing demolition to proceed despite evidence that the structure may have been a 19th-century schoolhouse relocated from Roslindale. The commission requested the builder salvage heavy timbers and authorized the updating of the historical record for the site.

items.title: 4 Grove Street
items.summary: Found the building preferably preserved due to its prominent corner location and character-defining porch. The architect stated the owner intends to restore the porch and siding to their original condition.

items.title: Determinations of Significance: 26 Rockwell Avenue and 76 Court Street
items.summary: Found both properties significant and scheduled public hearings for the following month. The commission noted the unique concrete block construction at Rockwell Avenue and the mid-19th-century architecture of Court Street.

items.title: Demolition Applications: 115 Emerald Street and 53 Winford Way
items.summary: Passed on review for both properties, waiving further interest in the demolition of the 1950s structures.

items.title: Routine Applications and Minutes
items.summary: Formally received demolition applications for 19 Curtis Street and 122-124 Woodruff Avenue, offered no comment on cell tower modifications at 121 Riverside Avenue and 20 Harvard Avenue, and approved the January meeting minutes.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Monument Restoration
items.summary: Approved a $2,500 allocation to fund the restoration of approximately 15 veteran headstones as part of a grant-funded pilot program.

items.title: Preservation Directives and Subcommittee
items.summary: Established a subcommittee to update overarching directives for demolition delays and to create expedited review processes for buildings constructed before 1900.

items.title: Salem Street Corridor Rezoning Discussion
items.summary: Discussed the potential impact of proposed up-zoning on a high concentration of pre-1900 buildings in East Medford. The commission agreed to draft a letter to the city requesting stakeholder status and recommending protections for character-defining structures within the corridor.

items.title: Survey and Planning Updates
items.summary: Received updates on the Sagamore Vale survey and authorized updating the inventory form for a historic property on Mystic Street associated with Reverend John Pierpont.
